title: Design System: NET
scope: Suspended Field is the target system, applied today only to the landing page `/` via `.world-field` (web/src/app/world-field.css). /docs and /games still run the legacy root @theme in web/src/app/globals.css until a planned second pass; do not extend the legacy theme.

ink-faint-on-panel.note: Re-declared as --color-ink-faint inside the slab utility; --color-ink-dim is not overridden on panels.

display.purpose: Hero area title only; uppercase; rises in line by line.

headline.purpose: Every section title; uppercase, max 15em; each line lifted into place on scroll.

body.purpose:
Prose in ink-dim, 14-15px, max 34-36em. All

in the world default to Archivo.

numeral.purpose: Measured figures in stat panels, with a 10px mono unit beside them.

label.purpose: Vertical section markers on the right pillar, panel IDs, document refs.

data.purpose: Event tails, code, ASCII diagrams, panel header bars.

shadows.name: panel-attended
shadows.purpose: Panel lifted on hover/focus, with a 5px rise.

shadows.name: seam-glow
shadows.purpose: Spill under the seam of an attended panel.

shadows.name: held-seam-glow
shadows.purpose: Spill under the seam of a held panel.

motion.name: ease-field
motion.purpose: The one easing for displacement and hold.

motion.name: attend
motion.value: translateY(-5px) 0.6s; border, face, ticks 0.35s; seam scaleX(0.3 -> 1) 0.7s
motion.purpose: Hover/focus lift: the field picks up what you attend to.

motion.name: altitude-rank
motion.value: static offsets above a shared floor hairline: 0 / 40px / 96px

motion.name: altitude-climb
motion.value: --climb = index x 14px, aligned to the bottom
motion.purpose: Migration phases: a staircase from snapshot to complete.

motion.name: field-wave
motion.value: translateY(-9px) peaking at 18%, 7s, delay = index x 0.28s
motion.purpose: Nine axioms: one wave in reading order, like a pingwave.

motion.name: field-sync
motion.purpose: Panels that are one live system (hero telemetry, the NET topology panel).

motion.name: lift-line
motion.value: translateY(0.5em) + blur(8px) -> none, 1.3s, 110ms stagger per line
motion.purpose: Section titles pushed into place on scroll; visible without script.

motion.name: scenery
motion.value: Monolith sway +/- 7deg over 14s with a 14px bob; Blackwall pillars bob
motion.purpose: Concrete scenery only; it carries no data, so it is exempt from the float rule.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All float, wave, sync, rise, lift and scenery loops drop to static.

components.name: Field Button
components.description: The one primary action (Install NET): a block of field light. It does not move; it lightens on hover and a green line lights below.
components.html: Install NET

components.name: Ghost Field Button
components.description: Secondary action: a transparent terminal ghost whose border and label turn field green on hover.

components.name: Field Link
components.description: Inline link in prose: ink text over a half-strength green underline that fills on hover.
components.html: Flagship use: agentic capability federation across a trusted mesh.

components.name: Lifting Panel
components.description: The terminal panel held in the field: corner ticks, scanlines, hairline border. Attention lifts it 5px, dims the border green and lights the seam.
components.html:
Drop, don't queue

Backpressure sheds load at the edge instead of building latency in the middle.

components.name: Section Title with Pillar Stencil
components.description: Monumental uppercase headline; the section marker is stencilled vertically down the right pillar, never above the heading.
components.html:
§03 / protocol properties

Nine axioms.
One runtime.

narrative.overview:
The mesh is a force field. The landing is a dark, raw-concrete brutalist hall, held up by nothing visible: shards, monoliths and pillars of cast concrete hang in it, lit by one cold light shaft through the dust. Inside that hall the information sits on **terminal panels**: near-black phosphor glass with a hairline border, faint scanlines and green corner ticks, the project's cyberpunk HUD surface. The concrete is the world; the terminal is the instrument.

Float carries meaning. The panels sit still on aligned grids by default, resting on the floor. A panel leaves the floor only when its height says something: altitude encodes speed (NET above real-time above best-effort), a staircase encodes progress (migration phases climbing to complete), a travelling wave encodes propagation (the nine axioms, like a pingwave), a shared rhythm encodes a single live system (the hero telemetry). Hovering a panel lifts it a few pixels and lights its seam: the field picks up what you attend to. The motion grammar is displacement and hold: **resting**, **attended** (lifted on hover/focus), **held** (seam always lit), **launched** (the hero canvas, where the cursor pushes shards and a click throws them).

The world is cyber-led and keeps the project's terminal telemetry, mono data and acid green, and refuses the dark-neon dev-tool page where every card floats, glows and differs for no reason.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials: procedural cast concrete for scenery, terminal glass for every panel.
Acid green carries one meaning: the field (live, held, attended, or the one primary action).
Monumental geometric caps (TeX Gyre Adventor, Avant Garde lineage) for titles; Archivo for prose; JetBrains Mono only for data, code, telemetry and controls.
Square corners. Panels on aligned, equal grids; height above the floor is data, never ornament.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Field Green means the field: live, held, attended, or the one primary action. On a panel it appears only as the corner ticks (where the field grips it, 60% at rest, full when attended), the dim border when attended, and the seam. It is never a panel fill, a section background or a full bright border at rest.

rules.name: The Panel Ink Rule
rules.body: Inside a panel, only the faint ink is raised (`ink-faint-on-panel`); dim and primary ink keep their ground values. Get it by putting text inside the `slab` utility, not by hand-picking a grey.

rules.name: The No Red Rule
rules.body: The palette has no red. Warnings are amber. Inherited terminal window dots are neutralised to grey and dim green inside the world.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Adventor for structure, Archivo for sentences, JetBrains Mono for anything a machine would print. Never set prose in mono, never set a number readout in Archivo.

rules.name: The Monument Rule
rules.body: Titles are bold, uppercase, negatively tracked and nearly solid (line-height under 1). A title that needs a period to land gets it ("NET. MOVES AT LIGHT.").

rules.name: The Meaningful Float Rule
rules.body: A panel leaves the floor only when its height encodes something: rank, progress, propagation, shared state, or the visitor's attention. If you can't say what the height means, the panel rests. No random bobs, no per-card offsets, no idle drift on panels. All of it stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: The field shows itself on a panel as a single 1px green line along its bottom edge: grown from 30% width when attended, or always lit when held. Held is reserved for the statement panel of a section.

rules.name: The Held Not Hung Rule
rules.body: Panels are never wired to each other, railed or framed together; a panel's relationship to the page is its grid position and its shadow on the floor. The only lines that join things are field threads between mesh nodes (the hero canvas, the Mikoshi route), and they are green because they are the field.

rules.name: The Two Materials Rule
rules.body: Concrete is for scenery: canvas shards, Monoliths, Mikoshi plinths, Blackwall pillars. Terminal glass is for anything that carries words or numbers. Never put text on concrete, never make scenery out of panels.

dos: **Do** scope new landing-world work under `.world-field` and build every text-bearing container from the `slab` utility, so the terminal face, corner ticks and raised faint ink (`#7f8479`) come with it.
**Do** lay panels on aligned, equal grids, one column per peer, same span and same top edge.
**Do** give a panel altitude only to encode rank, progress, propagation, shared state or attention.
**Do** move on the field ease (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`), and keep every float, wave, sync, rise and lift behind `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** label simulated telemetry as SIMULATED and measured figures as observed.
**Do** make concrete scenery with the procedural SVG textures (`--tex-grain`, `--tex-stain`, `--tex-pits`), not raster images.
donts: **Don't** extend the legacy root theme (Major Mono Display, Space Grotesk, CRT scanlines, `#3df0ff` cyan, `#ff5e3d` warn) on any new surface; it survives only until /docs and /games migrate.
**Don't** float, bob, offset or stagger a panel for variety; staggered spans, overlaps and edge bleeds are retired.
**Don't** put text on concrete or build panels out of concrete.
**Don't** use Field Green as a panel fill, section background or bright resting border.
**Don't** round corners on panels, buttons or terminals.
**Don't** use red, redaction bars, or `<<text>>` Board-style treatments.
**Don't** set prose in mono or titles in Archivo.
**Don't** wire, rail or frame panels together; only mesh nodes are joined, by green field threads.
